title: Terraform storage module: snapshot lifecycle, KMS defaults, and upgrade path
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a consolidated Terraform module that encodes our opinionated defaults for storage in Private (VPC) deployments: EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and S3 buckets. The module must provide safe snapshot lifecycle policies, KMS/default encryption key handling, cross-account snapshot copy hooks, and an upgrade-friendly interface so existing customers can opt into new defaults without data loss.

Goals:
- Enforce encryption-at-rest with a sensible default (Redwood-managed CMK) but allow customer-managed KMS to be supplied per-environment.
- Inspector-friendly snapshot lifecycle with automated retention tiers, verification job hooks (post-snapshot healthchecks), and soft-delete windows for accidental deletion recovery.
- Minimal, tested upgrade path: new module version should provide a migration plan for existing snapshot schedules and KMS rekeying without downtime.
- Provide CI checks and runtime healthchecks that operators can wire into Console dashboards (snapshot age distribution, failed snapshot jobs, kms errors).

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Default KMS: using a Redwood-managed multi-tenant CMK by default simplifies onboarding and enforces encryption, but customers in regulated environments must be able to opt for a customer-managed key (CMK). We will implement explicit boolean toggle and a kms_key_arn argument.
- Snapshot lifecycle policy: balance between cost and recoverability. Default retention is 30d daily + 365d monthly archive; configurable via variables. Automatic cross-region copy will be opt-in for customers with high DR needs.
- Soft-delete: snapshots will be tagged with lifecycle metadata and we will implement a configurable soft-delete window (default 72 hours) during which automated restore is possible. This increases storage costs slightly but substantially reduces accidental-data-loss incidents.
- Upgrade strategy: avoid in-place destructive changes. New defaults will be opt-in via a migration resource (terraform plan shows change), with a helper script to convert schedules and re-encrypt resources using customer-provided KMS.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for Terraform module using terratest (Go) and kitchen-terraform for integration checks on ephemeral AWS accounts.
- Post-deploy healthcheck lambda that validates latest snapshot timestamps, verifies snapshot integrity marker (checksum tag), and ensures KMS grants are intact. Healthcheck emits metrics to Console via CloudWatch/Prometheus export.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Storage+Module+Lifecycle+Design
- Terraform module registry preview: git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-modules.git//modules/storage?ref=feature/storage-retention
- Draft PR for initial module: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/347
- Dashboard prototype (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/storage-snapshots

Rollout plan:
1) Merge module behind feature flag in infra-modules repo.
2) Run migration job in staging clusters for sample customers (internal accounts).
3) Run smoke and restore tests.
4) Offer opt-in to production customers via migration guide + 30-day support window.

Open questions:
- Do we support automatic KMS re-encryption at scale or require customer action? (PM leaning toward semi-automated to reduce blast radius.)
- Should cross-account copy be a first-class variable or a separate module?

Risks:
- Re-encryption operations can be slow and expensive for large fleets; must be carefully throttled.
- Incorrect IAM policies for snapshot copy/KMS grants can cause silent failures.

Next steps:
- Finalize variables and outputs contract for module (who owns bucket policies vs module).
- Add terratest suite focused on KMS grants and snapshot integrity.
- Prepare migration runbook and support checklist.

acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables: enable_kms_default (bool), kms_key_arn (string), retention_daily_days (int), retention_monthly_days (int), soft_delete_window_hours (int)
Default deployment uses Redwood-managed CMK and enforces encryption for EBS/EFS/S3 unless kms_key_arn provided
Snapshot lifecycle policy created with tags and soft-delete window; snapshots older than retention are removed by lifecycle job
Post-deploy healthcheck lambda runs and reports metrics to Console; failing checks create an Ops alert
Migration guide published with step-by-step for customers to opt into new defaults without data loss
implementation_steps: Create initial Terraform module in infra-modules/modules/storage with variable contract and examples
Implement KMS handling: default to redwood-managed key, allow kms_key_arn override, and add kms_grant resource examples
Add snapshot lifecycle resource for EBS and EFS with configurable retention and soft-delete tagging
Add optional S3 lifecycle template for backups/archives and cross-region replication skeleton
Write terratest and kitchen-terraform tests focusing on encryption, snapshot creation, and lifecycle enforcement
Implement healthcheck lambda and dashboard shipper; wire CloudWatch metrics to Console
Draft migration runbook and customer-facing docs; perform internal staging migration
Iterate on feedback from security review and QA, then schedule opt-in rollout
